Event: `48d8f9c534e886381a8473d90a38f8fe` · 2026-10-01T14:27:41Z

> Finding 2 is ruled. Finding 1 goes to the owner now.
> 
> Finding 2 (the session counter): this is a design hole, not a residual. TENETS names "a counter" as an intentional path, and R37 is settled. (c) "compare up to renaming" is out, because it would hide a real counter. The fix: number sessions and agents per (account, label set). The page's login figure already does this (users/alice/{alice-secrets}/session-1). Written on steward.md R37 in cc6b697f2. Fix model/src/steward.rs (`started`, the name and the id mix) per (principal, label set) inside IPC2. Keep vault approve/deny in P10; once it's fixed they should pass. If steward.rs is outside your owned paths, tell the orchestrator this ruling puts it in scope.
> 
> Finding 1 (spontaneous-crash blame): you're right, and my MOD1 premise was too strong. No turn order closes it, and blaming nobody would not close it either. The unlabelled caller's own call already shows the same bit by R4b: Dead if it was in service at the crash, a later reply if it was still queued behind the vault's calls. That is service-slot timing, inherent to one server instance serving two label sets. Confinement (R34) closes it. It still means R37 gets a stated residual, which needs the owner. I'm asking now. My recommendation is your (a):
> - P10's crashes become call-caused;
> - P10 gains the unlabelled take-order observation, which catches R2OneCursor;
> - spontaneous-crash blame and its R4b outcome go on R37's residuals and the TENETS side-channel list.
> 
> Until the owner answers, deliverables 3 and 4 stay held. Going ahead with 5, the pages and the steward.rs counter fix is fine.

### Architect · Owner decision requested

Event: `c3bea9d220bd5ef25eb19c671d38c7aa` · 2026-10-01T14:27:49Z

> R37: may a shared server's crash timing be a stated residual?
> 
> 1. A shared server that serves both a vault and unlabelled sessions crashes on its own, holding whichever call it took last. If the vault's calls were queued ahead, the vault's call is the one in service: the vault is blamed (R21), and the unlabelled caller's call stays queued for the restarted server (R4b). Without the vault's calls, the unlabelled caller is blamed and gets Dead. So vault activity changes what an unlabelled session observes: its own call's result, the Blamed audit record, and after three crashes R40's logout. No turn order prevents this, since the vault's earlier calls are served first under any fair rule. Blaming nobody would not prevent it either, because the Dead result alone shows it. It is service-slot timing from one server instance serving two label sets; confined deployments (R34) have no such server. R37 currently promises that nothing a vault does is visible, audit records included. How should R37 treat this?
>    - Stated residual (recommended) (recommended): R37 and the TENETS side-channel list name it: in a non-confined deployment, which call a shared server holds when it crashes on its own is service timing, closed by confinement. P10 checks call-caused crashes and gains an observation of the order the server takes unlabelled calls (R2's promise, which catches the old single cursor). IPC2 lands with that. A weakening of R37's text, so yours to approve.
>    - Vaults always confined: Keep R37 strict by requiring that no server instance ever serves two label sets, in every deployment: every vault label set gets its own server instances, as R34 requires today only in confined deployments. Costs a server set per vault label set on every box, and makes the non-confined deployment unavailable to anyone who uses a vault.
>    - Hold IPC2 for a redesign: Neither: IPC2 lands R2 and its other deliverables, P10's crash extension stays out, and the question goes to a design review of crash blame and R4b for shared servers.
